text_blocks.snippet: Federal prosecutors and the Better Business Bureau warn Central Illinois residents about active phone and text impersonation scams.

list.snippet: Federal/Legal Imposter Calls: Scammers spoof numbers and pretend to be attorneys from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois , demanding immediate payment or threats of arrest.
Traffic/Toll Smishing Texts: Fake texts claim you owe money for toll or traffic violations, mimicking the Illinois Department of Transportation or DMV.
Utility "Slamming": Callers claim to be with Energy Choice or local utilities, tricking schools and businesses into changing or revealing current rates.
Package Delivery Texts: Fraudulent texts claim a package delivery is stuck due to a missing address number, requesting credit card info or a link click.
Hang up immediately: Government agencies never call or text demanding instant payment or financial details.
Practice the pause: Take time to verify urgent requests independently rather than acting under pressure.
Never click links: Avoid unsolicited links in texts or emails regarding fines or deliveries.
Federal/Local Crimes: Report to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center or call 1-800-225-5324.
Consumer Fraud: Contact the Illinois Attorney General's Scam Hotline at 1-800-243-0618.
Local Inquiries: Reach out to the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois.
